result.response:
I have resolved the issue where email messages crashed on non-ASCII hostnames/domains when the email encoding was non-unicode.

### Cause
When the computer's hostname contains non-ASCII characters, [`socket.getfqdn()`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py) returns a unicode string. When generating default `Message-ID` headers, [`make_msgid(domain=DNS_NAME)`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L260) incorporated this unicode hostname into the header value. For emails with non-UTF-8 encodings (such as `iso-8859-1`), header sanitization via [`forbid_multi_line_headers`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L55) attempted to encode the non-ASCII `Message-ID` with the email's charset, raising a `UnicodeEncodeError`.

### Solution
1. In [`django/core/mail/utils.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L17), updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/utils.py#L14-L17) to punycode-encode non-ASCII domain names using `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`.
2. In [`django/core/mail/message.py`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L258-L268), ensured that `DNS_NAME` passed to [`make_msgid`](file:///testbed/django/core/mail/message.py#L268) is safely converted to punycode if it contains non-ASCII characters.
